comparisons.peer_topic: Net interest income and yield performance in 2024
comparisons.peer_summary: Net interest income decreased by $871 million to $56.1 billion in 2024 compared to 2023, with net interest yield on a fully taxable-equivalent basis dropping 13 basis points to 1.95 percent. These declines were primarily driven by higher deposit costs, which were partially offset by higher asset yields and increased net interest income from Global Markets activity.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPM and BAC report on the performance of their net interest yield (a key measure of interest-earning assets) in 2024, but they present opposing trends in yield direction and underlying drivers. JPM reported that its net yield on an FTE basis decreased by 7 basis points to 2.63%, driven by balance sheet actions and reinvestments, whereas BAC reported a larger decrease of 13 basis points to 1.95%, primarily driven by higher deposit costs. JPM explicitly notes its net yield excluding Markets was flat, while BAC highlights that higher asset yields partially offset the deposit cost increases.

comparisons.peer_topic: Net Interest Income Growth and Drivers
comparisons.peer_summary: Net interest income for 2024 was $8.06 billion, representing a 27% increase from 2023, driven by higher interest income from trading assets, investments, and collateralized agreements due to higher balances and rates, partially offset by a decrease in deposits with banks.
comparisons.comparison: JPM and GS both disclose the movement in their net interest metrics for 2024, but they highlight opposite directions for Net Interest Income (NII). JPM’s disclosure context indicates NII increased, supported by a higher yield on average interest-earning assets (up 36 bps to 5.50%). In contrast, GS reports its NII increased by 27% to $8.06 billion, driven by higher interest income from trading assets and investments due to higher rates and balances, but does not report an asset yield increase in the same sentence; instead, GS emphasizes that this income growth was partly offset by an increase in interest expense related to collateralized financings and deposits.

sentences.text: The Firm's average interest-earning assets were $3.5 trillion, up $212 billion, and the yield was 5.50%, up 36 bps.
The net yield on these assets, on an FTE basis, was 2.63%, a decrease of 7 bps.

Net interest income in the consolidated statements of earnings was $8.06 billion for 2024, 27% higher than 2023, reflecting an increase in interest income, partially offset by an increase in interest expense.

The increase in interest income primarily related to trading assets and investments (each reflecting the impact of higher average balances and higher average interest rates), collateralized agreements and other interest-earning assets (each reflecting the impact of higher average interest rates), partially offset by a decrease in interest income related to deposits with banks (reflecting the impact of lower average balances).
